# Owned Evidence-file JSON acquisition

These fixtures qualify a finite Linux component profile of the frozen
`rea-agents@6.8.0` file reader. The frozen npm tarball SHA-256 is
`8d542ec76a9cb350584b60a6c9c088706ff812d5bb5b094c20c95b6dc25698bb`.
The primary 19-case producer capture verified all 2,398 installed package files
against that tarball before running the original code.

## Original references

`reference-r2.json` contains 19 actual calls to the original `readJsonFile`,
including complete typed and public projected errors. Fourteen cases agree
within the implemented profile: bare Evidence, a canonical bundle, duplicate
keys/property order, JavaScript numeric semantics, a complete file exceeding
8 MiB, empty/whitespace JSON, UTF-8/BOM failures, missing paths and three
nonregular file types. The bare record and bundle also pass the independent
owned Evidence authenticator in the Rust test.

Five cases remain explicit native profile gaps: a general V8 grammar diagnostic,
an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate, a nonfinite parsed number, nesting depth 121 and
following a symlink. They are not counted as reference-equivalent successes.

`access-reference-r1.json` adds real original reads that fail with EACCES
(the producer ran as uid 1000 against an owned mode-000 file) and ENAMETOOLONG.
It preserves their complete original projections. The native tests independently
exercise those filesystem conditions; permission assertions are conditional on
a non-root test process. The producer restores its owned permission fixture to
mode 0600 afterward. A replay must recreate the intended mode-000 condition.

The 8 MiB boundary is an original parser implementation threshold, not a file
size limit. The large positive fixture has exactly 8,392,715 input bytes. It is
generated by the recipe in the reference, then checked against its original
input SHA-256 and complete original serialized-value SHA-256. The repository
does not retain a redundant multi-megabyte literal fixture.

The two small complete Evidence inputs are stored as `bare-record.json` and
`canonical-bundle.json`. Small malformed/token inputs are encoded in the
reference's hex fields. `producer/` preserves the original runners, requests
and receipts; historical paths are not rewritten.

## Caller interface

`read_json(path, roots, cancellation, ownership, NativeJsonLimits)` consumes its
path and roots and returns `OwnedJson { value, object_order, selected_path,
input_bytes, sha256 }`. The ownership argument is generic `G: Send + 'static`;
the runtime passes its Arc holding the effect-owner admission and bounded
semaphore permit.

The helper opens the source below configured roots with descriptor-relative
lookups and no symlink traversal. It holds one source descriptor through reads,
parsing, same-descriptor checks, a confined final pathname identity check and
close. Small inputs get a bounded-memory UTF-8 scan before parsing, preserving
the original native-parser UTF-8/BOM priority; both reads use the same descriptor
and their content digests must agree. Large inputs are decoded incrementally.
There is no complete input byte vector or complete document string.

A single blocking task owns this entire operation. Dropping the async waiter
notifies the task through a child cancellation token; the real admission guard
remains in the task until it finishes. Read cancellation is checked around each
bounded descriptor read and during value assembly. This is cooperative
cancellation, including kernel calls, and does not promise a hard deadline for
a stuck filesystem operation.

The parallel metadata tree preserves actual JavaScript own-property order,
including numeric index names and first insertion position when a duplicate
key replaces its value. Replacing a duplicate object with a scalar also removes
the obsolete metadata subtree. `object_order.keys(path)` is a trusted
record/file-relative resolver for `rea_evidence_source`; caller-provided metadata
has no role.

Every numeric token is interpreted as an IEEE-754 JavaScript Number before
choosing its serde representation. Integral representable values normalize
1.0/1e0 and negative zero to integers; oversized integers are rounded to f64
first. The helper does not retain the extra precision of serde u64 parsing.

## Typed outcomes and original mapping

`FileReadError::File` carries `FileReason` and a captured errno.
`FileReason::as_str()` returns the original reason spelling:

| Fact | Original reason |
| --- | --- |
| ENOENT or ENOTDIR | missing |
| ENAMETOOLONG | path-limit |
| Independently established nonregular selection | not-file |
| Other physical errors, including EACCES and EPERM | io |

An invalid UTF-8/BOM/empty-input outcome carries the exact original content issue
message and optional user-message override. The parent must distinguish
invalid-json from a schema-invalid Evidence record: the original invalid-json
projection uses evidence_integrity_mismatch with execution_failure, while
wrong-kind uses invalid_request. The complete original error envelopes in these
fixtures are the parent service's comparison oracle.

Unknown V8 grammar messages and valid JavaScript values that serde cannot
represent are `NativeProfileGap`, not fabricated original diagnostics.
The default native materialization estimate is 128 MiB, encoded token limit
16 MiB and depth limit 120. These are declared native admission limits; the
materialization estimate is not a hard allocator/RSS measurement. They do not
establish complete original heap-headroom equivalence.

Close errors preserve the primary failure and
`native_cleanup_incomplete: true`; they are not rewritten as cancellation with
successful cleanup. This Linux profile closes a numeric descriptor once and
never retries that number after close. See the Linux
[close(2) documentation](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/close.2.html).
No kernel close-failure injection or full REA retained cleanup/retry capability
is claimed. Non-Linux close-lifecycle support remains an explicit profile gap.

## Qualification

Eight component tests and strict Clippy passed with Rust 1.95.0, edition 2021,
offline and two build jobs. Dependency identities match the root lockfile.
Tests use real confined files, real permissions/path limits, a real semaphore
permit held after waiter abort, ordinary file-write/grow/truncate/name-replace
fences, split UTF-8 scalars, parser limits, and the frozen original reference.

The semantic/source authenticator and same-descriptor comparison use the
actual pinned production code. No runtime effect-admission substitute is claimed:
the component uses a real semaphore guard through the generic owner interface,
and the parent runtime separately instantiates its full effect-owner guard.
Public MCP, runtime roots, final error envelopes and retained session behavior
still require the parent's actual binary qualification.

The original r1 reference capture stopped at an overlong owned Unix-socket
fixture path before starting Node; its files/logs remain preserved externally.
The successful r2 capture used a distinct owned short socket directory. The r1
component passed all eight tests but failed three style lints; r2 corrected those
lints and passed both gates. No failed attempt was relabeled successful.
